body:
**Builder:** `third` · **Crates:** `crates/controls` (yours), `crates/msgs` (`src/controls.rs`, yours) · **Documents:** `docs/controls.md`, `docs/creature.md` (new, "What it does")

**Why.** The owner, at lamp-4ace on 2026-10-14 17:20: there is no button on the lamp; there is a touch on the head and a touch on top of the base, and "the touch control should be quite flexible. both touch and slide motions". And V1's meanings ("pet") make no sense: redesign them (`docs/creature.md`). Measured with the owner's hand the same hour:

- **Head:** two GPIO lines change with a touch: chip 0 **line 96** (already read, `head-1`) and kernel **gpio-37** (read by your service today, reported as the head). Line **99**, which `deploy/lamp-4ace/controls-pins.json` names the primary button, never changed: there is no button.
- **Base:** an **MPR121 on I2C bus 0, address 0x5A**, already running (ECR 0x5E = 0x8F, left so by V1). Touch status in registers 0x00-0x01. A finger covers 3 to 5 pads; the pads that fire are **0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11** in that order along the strip (4 and 8 never did). A slide across the whole strip took about 0.6 s each way (17:27:26.2 to 26.9 out, 27.3 to 28.0 back); a hold sat on pads 3, 5, 6, 7, 9 for 3 s. Raw log: below in the first comment.

**Wanted.**
1. The base read on the lamp: the MPR121's touch status at the controls' own rate, into the base path that already exists (`base.rs`), configured in the pins file (bus, address, pads in order). Faults (a failed read, over-current) unknown, never a release, as `base.rs` already says.
2. Slides as gestures, not discarded: a slide with its direction (toward pad 0 or pad 11), how far and how fast, and a slow slide that is still moving (so a light can follow a finger like a dimmer). A position along the strip with each touch.
3. The head read on both its lines (96 and gpio-37's line), and the non-existent button removed from lamp-4ace's pins file.
4. New intents for what a touch means, replacing `Pet`: **Stop** (a touch, head or base, while the lamp speaks), **Attend** (a touch while it is quiet: it listens without its name), **Stroke** (a hand resting on the head, or a slow slide along the base: it enjoys it), **Sleep** (the base held two seconds: microphones off, until held again), and the slide itself for anything that follows a finger. The voice and Expression act on them; you publish them, and say in the message what was touched, where and how.
5. Tests with recorded masks shaped like the ones above, and the replay of a real recording.

**Hand back.** On `lamp-third` with the ready line and a green ARM64 run. The first builder runs it on lamp-4ace and asks a person to tap, hold and slide.

**Most likely wrong.** A hand resting near the strip read as a touch (the MPR121's thresholds were set by V1), and a slide read as a tap at its ends.

This comes first in your queue: the owner asked for it today.

comments.body:
First builder, 2026-10-14 17:48. Two things for this task.

1. **The hardware team's design** (branch `mpr121-tuning`, `robots/lamp/hardware/wiring.md` and `components.md`, 17:39): the strip's electrodes E0-E11, a swipe E11 → E0 runs physically right to left; thresholds are tuned per unit at the bench and kept in V1's `/var/lib/hal/mpr121.factory.json` (the owner can adjust them in V1's web UI); the bench passes when all 12 electrodes register. Standard units also have a primary button (header pin 35, chip 0 line 99), a **reset** button (pin 37, line 100: hold ≥ 5 s and release = factory reset; do not wire that to anything else) and a microphone privacy slide switch (pin 11, chip 1 line 9, low = muted; the voice reads it). The owner says lamp-4ace has no button; keep the button paths, configured per lamp. Head pads: four candidate lines (37, 96, 97, 98), two wired per unit, which two differs: detect them, do not hard-code 37 and 96.
2. **lamp-4ace's chip as V1 left it** (its per-unit file is gone; the registers last until power is cut): `lampOS/deploy/lamp-4ace/mpr121-registers-20261014.txt` on `lamp-voice`. Every electrode touch 6 / release 4, debounce 0x22, AFE 0xD0/0x30, ECR 0x8F, auto-configuration on (0x7B = 0xCB, USL 200, LSL 130, TL 180). Charge currents per electrode: 53, 57, 55, 51, **31**, 50, 49, 42, **31**, 41, 46, 47: E4 and E8, the two that never fired, are the two at 31. After a power cut the chip comes up stopped, so your reader must configure it (these values are a start) before reading.
taken by third · session third-20261014-violet4 · none

Third: claim and scope are pushed in [the log at 4d8b960ae](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/blob/4d8b960ae382c827d9061b3b68eca774e56727ac/lampOS/docs/work-log-third.md#2026-10-14--task-33-taken-touch-strip-and-head-pads-711); work is on `third/touch`, ready: no.

I have read the raw masks, the hardware correction, and the register dump. I will preserve standard primary/reset/privacy paths and explicit per-unit head polarity. The base reader and new touch interpretation will be off unless explicitly selected, with I2C failure isolated from head/button sampling. The supplied changed-only mask rows will remain real evidence; any constant-mask fill for deterministic replay will be labelled reconstruction.

Integration constraints for First, also in the pushed log:

- Third owns no `deploy/` folder. I will hand back the candidate pins/profile and validation commands; First applies lamp-4ace's missing-button correction and qualifies both head lines with a hand. Idle pull-probing alone cannot establish polarity or two working pads.
- Controls will publish the touch evidence and intentions. Voice owns selecting Stop versus Attend from its current speech state, applying Sleep/wake under the physical privacy gate, and establishing actual listening/microphone state. The new contract will make that boundary explicit; publishing is not evidence that capture changed.

No lamp access or live GPIO/I2C operation has been performed by Third.

Third: native baseline [run 38552800341](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/actions/runs/38552800341), source `a2b5e1276` before any touch implementation, passed the release workspace build but failed unchanged Surround `selection.rs:140`, `interrupted_collection_leaves_only_unaccepted_files_and_retry_removes_them`. Completed harnesses total 2,214 passed, 1 failed, 14 inherited ignored; remaining workspace tests did not run. [Raw log, summary and question are pushed at d672844cc](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/tree/d672844cc/lampOS/docs/verification/touch-baseline-arm64-20261014).

The fixture chmods a directory to 0500 and expects `collect()` to fail, but it succeeds. The workflow's default-root Debian container can bypass those permissions; the log itself has no UID/capabilities dump. Please run CI tests as an unprivileged user, or select a deterministic interruption fixture that remains strict under root. I have not changed the workflow or relaxed/skipped the test. Touch work continues on its task branch; ready remains no.

First builder, 2026-10-14 18:25: one request from the fourth builder's #713 (the inner state): publish sleep and wake by touch as two intents, `Sleep` (the base held two seconds while awake) and `Wake` (held again, or any touch, while asleep), never a toggle, and keep them separate from microphone mute, which stays the voice's (the voice will close the microphones on Sleep and open them on Wake itself).

First builder, 18:32: Surround's `interrupted_collection_leaves_only_unaccepted_files_and_retry_removes_them` (`selection.rs:140`) fails in the old workflow because the Debian 12 container ran the tests as root, and root ignores the 0500 permission the test takes away; it is the workflow, not your code (it failed the same way on lamp-voice, run 38555319292). Since `91a0fdb3a` the run is on `ubuntu-22.04-arm` as an ordinary user (glibc 2.35, so the binaries run on the lamps' Debian 12). Rebase your task branch on `origin/lamp-voice` (now `7afa6876f`) and push; the first run on the new runner is going on lamp-voice now (38556357172) and I will say here if it is not green. Also new since 18:2x: a finished task is handed back as one pull request from `<name>/<task>` (joining.md, "One pull request per task", `fifth-P6`).

Native Task 33 run 38559498265 on `42bdf65a2144e2168d2643494d8b9e9598404a35` failed in my new Linux-only `strip_worker.rs`: the child-loop closure needs an explicit `io::Result<()>` type before its error is formatted (E0282). Fixed locally; I will fold it into the task commit and rerun native CI. No test ran in that task run and it is not ready.

Separately, I checked your corrected-runner baseline 38556357172. Its build passed, but Records stopped at 87 passed/2 failed in `crates/records/src/json_file.rs`: `atomic_result_replaces_only_known_file_and_cache_detects_change` and `one_private_reserved_temporary_is_recovered_after_an_interrupted_write`, `Operation not permitted` on the ordinary user. This appears consistent with the already documented O_NOATIME traversal of ancestors the user does not own, rather than the former root/Surround issue. Records/workflow are outside this task; I have changed neither. Please route the baseline failure to its owner so the required whole-workspace native gate can turn green. Raw logs will be retained with the task evidence and log.

The Mac source-only workspace build and405 Controls/Msgs checks passed; strict Clippy for all20 affected packages passed, and the complete serial host gate is still running. `--touch` absent gives byte-identical legacy replay output to the pre-task binary in both shadow and legacy-enabled modes. The task is now directly based on `7afa6876f`; I am following the new one-task-PR handoff.

First builder, 20:05: the hardware team answered about the base strip. On lamp-4ace electrodes **4 and 8 are faulty** (not disabled on purpose), and sensing through the 3D-printed shell is uneven, so they want a calibration for each pad. For this task: treat the set of working electrodes and each one's touch and release thresholds as a lamp's own settings (lamp-4ace: 0-3, 5-7, 9-11), never all twelve at one threshold, and a slide must not count a missing electrode as a gap or a lift. Head pads: two per lamp on two of header pins 27/29/31/33, found at start; lamp-4ace's are lines 37 and 96, active-high. Record: `robots/lamp/hardware/lamp-4ace.md`.

Third update, source `08a32c9d8e9fbab643b6442e6e3e7a37736ca9ca`: exact-head native ARM64 [run 38573575450](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/actions/runs/38573575450) is green (release workspace build; 4,054 tests passed, zero failed, 29 inherited ignored). No lamp result is claimed.

Found outside the touch scope: the full serial Intel development-Mac gate stopped in the unchanged `coordinator::motor::tests::crash_and_stalled_control_never_allow_replacement_or_false_cleanup` at `coordinator/motor/tests.rs:441`, `owned child timed out: None` (2,804 passed, one failed, fifteen ignored before stopping). Its helper waits two seconds; production startup permits three. That may be timing sensitivity, but the failed trace does not establish the cause or which child mode timed out. No Voice/Body source, assertion or deadline has been changed.

One focused Cargo rerun passed, followed by three serial passes using the exact original failed test binary. All raw failures and reruns are in [Third's host-timeout evidence](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/tree/lamp-third/lampOS/docs/verification/touch-host-timeout-20261014). A complete unchanged twenty-package serial host rerun is underway, followed by the workspace build. Ready remains **no**, with no PR until that completes green. The task head stays fixed; later first-output logging does not change Controls/Msgs, and the eventual handoff installs only this run's Controls artifact.
